content: 1. Momelotinib increases the toxicity of tenofovir alafenamide (AF) through competition for plasma protein binding. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 2. Momelotinib, a breast cancer resistance protein (BCRP) inhibitor, may increase the exposure of BCRP substrates, potentially raising the risk of adverse reactions. Dose adjustments for other BCRP substrates may be necessary, and close monitoring is advised. 3. Nirmatrelvir increases the levels or effects of tenofovir AF by altering hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is required. Co-administration may lead to increased systemic exposure to tenofovir. 4. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases the levels or effects of tenofovir AF by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is required. Co-administration may increase systemic exposure to tenofovir. 5. Orlistat decreases the levels or effects of tenofovir AF by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is required. Loss of virological control has been reported in HIV-infected patients taking orlistat concomitantly. The exact mechanism is unclear but may involve a drug-drug interaction that inhibits systemic absorption of the antiretroviral drug. HIV RNA levels should be monitored frequently, and orlistat should be discontinued if an increased HIV viral load is confirmed. 6. Otesaconazole increases the levels or effects of tenofovir AF through mechanisms involving BCRP inhibition. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. Otesaconazole may increase the effects and toxicity risks of BCRP substrates. The lowest starting dose of the BCRP substrate should be used, or the dose should be reduced. 7. Regorafenib increases the levels or effects of tenofovir AF by likely inhibiting BCRP (ABCG2) transport. Co-administration with a BCRP substrate may increase systemic exposure to the substrate and related toxicity. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 8. Safinamide increases the levels or effects of tenofovir AF by inhibiting intestinal BCRP. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is required. BCRP substrates should be monitored for increased pharmacologic or adverse effects. 9. Sarecycline increases the levels or effects of tenofovir AF by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (P-gp) efflux transporters. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is required. Toxicities of P-gp substrates should be monitored, and dosage reductions may be necessary when co-administered with P-gp inhibitors. 10. Sotorasib decreases the levels or effects of tenofovir AF by inducing P-gp efflux transporters. Alternative drugs should be used. If unavoidable, refer to the prescribing information of the P-gp substrate for dosage modifications. 11. Stiripentol increases the levels or effects of tenofovir AF by inhibiting BCRP transport. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is required. Dosage reductions for BCRP substrates should be considered if adverse effects occur during co-administration. 12. Tafamidis increases the levels or effects of tenofovir AF by inhibiting BCRP in vitro, which may increase exposure to BCRP substrates following tafamidis or tafamidis meglumine administration. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is required. Dosage adjustments for BCRP substrates may be necessary. 13. Tafamidis meglumine increases the levels or effects of tenofovir AF by inhibiting BCRP in vitro, which may increase exposure to BCRP substrates following tafamidis or tafamidis meglumine administration. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is required. Dosage adjustments for BCRP substrates may be necessary. 14. Tepotinib increases the levels or effects of tenofovir AF by inhibiting P-gp efflux transporters. Alternative drugs should be used. If concomitant use is unavoidable, reduce the P-gp substrate dosage as recommended in its approved product labeling. 15. Tucatinib increases the levels or effects of tenofovir AF by inhibiting P-gp efflux transporters. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is required. Dosage reductions for P-gp substrates should be considered, especially where minimal concentration changes may lead to serious or life-threatening toxicities. 16. Vadadustat increases the levels or effects of tenofovir AF by increasing exposure to BCRP substrates. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is required. Signs of adverse effects of BCRP substrates should be monitored, and substrate doses should be reduced in accordance with their product labeling. 17. Voclosporin and tenofovir AF may increase each other's toxicity through nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. Co-administration with drugs associated with nephrotoxicity may increase the risk of acute and/or chronic nephrotoxicity. 18. In animal studies, no adverse developmental effects were observed when tenofovir alafenamide was administered during organogenesis at exposure levels equal to or up to 51 times the recommended daily dose in rats and rabbits, respectively. 19. It is unknown if tenofovir alafenamide is distributed in human breast milk. The developmental and health benefits of breastfeeding should be considered alongside the mother’s clinical need for the drug and any potential adverse effects on the breastfed infant from the drug or the underlying maternal condition. 20. Tenofovir alafenamide is generally acceptable for use during pregnancy. Controlled studies in pregnant women show no evidence of fetal risk. 21. Patients should be informed to take tenofovir alafenamide with food and adhere to a regular dosing schedule to avoid missed doses, as this can result in the development of resistance. 22. Tenofovir alafenamide should be stored at controlled room temperature (<30°C or 86°F) in its original container with the lid tightly closed. 23.
